hints: Look at the functional group in each structure and ask what type of intermolecular force each one can make.
Y is an ester with no O-H bond, X is a carboxylic acid that can hydrogen bond, and Z is an ionic salt.
Rank covalent molecules with weak forces lowest, hydrogen bonded molecules in the middle, and ionic lattices needing the most energy to separate highest.
walkthrough:
**Identify what X, Y and Z are**

X is butanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. Y is an ester, methyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. Z is a salt, sodium butanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$.

All have four carbons, so chain length is similar. The difference in boiling point must come from the functional group.

**Compare the strongest forces in each**

Y (ester) has permanent dipole-dipole attractions but cannot donate hydrogen bonds because it has no O-H or N-H bond. This gives relatively weak intermolecular forces.

X (carboxylic acid) can both donate and accept hydrogen bonds, and even forms stable dimers. Hydrogen bonding is much stronger than the dipole-dipole forces in Y.

**Spot why the salt is special**

Z is ionic. It is held together by strong ion-ion attractions in a lattice, not just simple molecular forces:
$$\text{COO}^- \text{ --- } \text{Na}^+ \text{ ionic attraction}$$
Far more energy is needed to break these attractions than to separate neutral molecules, so Z has by far the highest melting and boiling point.

Therefore lowest to highest is Y then X then Z.

options.A: Incorrect. This puts X lowest, but the carboxylic acid X can hydrogen bond strongly, so it boils much higher than the ester Y which has only dipole-dipole forces.
options.B: Correct. Y (ester, dipole-dipole only) is lowest, X (carboxylic acid, hydrogen bonding) is middle, and Z (ionic salt, ion-ion attractions) is highest. This matches the strength of forces to overcome on boiling.
options.C: Incorrect. This puts Z lowest and Y highest, which is backwards. The ionic compound Z has the strongest forces, not the weakest, and the ester Y cannot hydrogen bond so cannot be highest.
options.D: Incorrect. This correctly puts Z at one end but reverses X and Y. Students choosing this may think the acid is more volatile, but hydrogen bonding in X makes its boiling point higher than the ester Y.
